Anyway, I hope everyone is fine. Please remind me, who is bringing the tea and mandazi for Saturday? I can bring sugar. Also, if someone has a charger for a Tecno phone, I left mine at home. You can reach me on [PHONE]. Okay, see you soon, bye bye.

Hi team, Person5 here, reporting from the Person6 women's group meeting in Place4. Today was our monthly table banking day. Twenty-five members attended out of thirty. Together they saved eighteen thousand shillings, and we gave out four small loans to members who are starting businesses, mostly selling vegetables and second-hand clothes. The treasurer, Mama Person4, recorded everything in the book. Our next meeting is on the fifteenth. If you need the records, Person4's number is [PHONE].

Morning everyone, this is Person8. Yesterday we went to Place5 for the menstrual hygiene session with the girls in class six to eight. Sixty girls attended. We talked about periods, how to use and dispose of pads safely, and why they should not miss school. At the end, every girl received a pack of reusable sanitary pads. The head teacher, Mrs. Person7, has asked us to come back and also talk to the mothers. Her phone number is [PHONE] if someone wants to follow up.

Hello team, it's Person10. I want to share about the community dialogue on gender-based violence we held this afternoon at the chief's camp in Place3. Thirty-five women attended, plus a few village elders. The police gender desk officer, Corporal Person9, explained how to report cases and where survivors can get help. Some women shared their stories, it was very emotional. Three women asked for private follow-up, and we connected them with the counsellor. For anything about this session, you can call me on [PHONE].
